WH_SITE_ID.description: WhiteHat Sentinel site id (the per-application scan target). Resolves metadata via GET /api/site/{site_id} with a /api/site list-and-filter fallback, then fetches vulnerabilities via GET /api/vuln?query_site={site_id}. Each site becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip; hostname = '{siteLabel}@{site_id}').

WH_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Minimum severity floor — vulnerabilities normalised below this bucket are dropped before they reach Faraday. One of info / low / medium / high / critical (defaults to info, i.e. no floor). Applied after normalising WhiteHat's numeric severity scale (5 critical / 4 high / 3 medium / 2 low / 1 info) and its text enum (Critical / Urgent / High / Medium / Low / Note), with CVSS v3 / v2 base-score bucketing as a fallback when neither is present.

name: whitehat_sentinel
title: WhiteHat Sentinel
description: WhiteHat Sentinel REST API importer (legacy product — now Black Duck Continuous Dynamic; this executor is kept for orgs still on the WhiteHat-branded SaaS where the v2 endpoint shapes are unchanged). Pulls Dynamic Application Security Testing findings from a WhiteHat Sentinel tenant and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON to stdout. Authenticates against Sentinel with the WH_API_KEY env var — sent both as the canonical ``key=<WH_API_KEY>`` query parameter AND as an ``X-API-Key: <WH_API_KEY>`` header so tenants fronted by proxies that strip one form still authenticate. A pre-built 'Bearer <token>' value in WH_API_KEY short-circuits the API-key scheme and is forwarded as the Authorization header verbatim — useful for OAuth-gateway-fronted tenants after the Black Duck Continuous Dynamic migration. Resolves per-site metadata via GET /api/site/{site_id} (with a GET /api/site list-and-filter fallback for tenants that disable the per-id endpoint) so the host description surfaces siteLabel / url / target / status / open + closed vuln counts. Fetches per-site vulnerabilities via GET /api/vuln paginated with ``page`` (1-based) + ``page_size``, scoped via ``query_site=<site_id>`` and with ``display_attack_vectors`` / ``display_solution`` / ``display_description`` set so the rich fields ride inline (no per-vuln detail round-trip required). Each WhiteHat site becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because WhiteHat reports target URLs, not IPs; hostname = '{siteLabel}@{site_id}'); per-vuln findings attach as Faraday vulnerabilities — one per vuln id with [DAST] engine prefix, '{className} in {location}' in the title, class / severity / risk / cvssScore / vector / raw status / mitigationStatus / found / firstFound / opened / closed / lastTested / notes / siteId / siteLabel / attackVectors metadata in the description; solution / remediation / fix_recommendation / recommendation surfaces as Faraday resolution. Refs include CWE-* (single + list + list-of-dict shapes with the CWE- prefix collapsed, deduped), WASC-* (single + list shapes — Web Application Security Consortium taxonomy, surfaced by the legacy WhiteHat product), references / external_references / links URLs (string + dict.url + dict.href shapes), advisory_url. CVE list harvested from cve / cveId / cve_id (string) + cves / aliases / references (list of strings + list of dicts with cve / cveId / cve_id / name / id / value keys), plus a CVE-shaped name / title / summary token fallback. Severity normalised from WhiteHat's numeric 1-5 scale (5 critical / 4 high / 3 medium / 2 low / 1 info / 0 info) and its text enum (Critical / Urgent / High / Medium / Low / Note — also accepts Major / Important / Moderate / Minor / Informational / Information / Negligible / Trivial / None / Unspecified) with CVSS v3 / v2 base-score bucketing as a fallback when neither shape is present (≤0/>10 → info, <4 low, <7 medium, <9 high, ≥9 critical); client-side WH_MIN_SEVERITY floor enforced after normalisation. Status mapped from vuln.status (open / new / reopened → open, closed / fixed / patched → closed, mitigated / accepted / ignored / suppressed / muted / false_positive / invalid / not_applicable → risk-accepted) combined with per-vuln analyst-triage flags — ignored / muted / suppressed / falsePositive / accepted / mitigated (wins over lifecycle status), fixed / resolved → closed. WH_HOST is the Sentinel base URL (e.g. https://sentinel.whitehatsec.com); the bare hostname is prefixed with https://, hosts already pointing at .../api are accepted as-is (the /api segment is stripped before the canonical {base}/api/site and {base}/api/vuln URLs assemble).
